summary: @servicetitan/notifications 41.3.2 ships preinstall dropper that executes obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun runtime
details: The tarball for this version adds two files not part of the notifications library — setup.mjs and math_init.js — and declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". On npm install, setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/..., extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and uses that freshly downloaded alien runtime to execute the sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line Bun-CJS bundle heavily obfuscated with a shuffled string/integer array indexed by a rotation function and hex-named identifiers (canonical string-array-obfuscator output); it is not referenced by dist/index.js and is only reachable through the preinstall hook. The package advertises itself as a React notifications UI library; a UI library has no legitimate reason to fetch a second runtime and execute a large obfuscated payload at install. Invoking the payload through Bun rather than Node is consistent with evading Node-based install-time scanners. src/ and dist/ contain the expected notifications library code, indicating a trojanized publish rather than a legitimate release: attacker-controlled code runs on every consumer's machine during npm install of this version.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
